requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node2 and node3, each listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: inventory_app.py deployed as systemd service on both nodes, verified active and returning JSON with correct backend hostname via curl to 127.0.0.1:8080/health on each node; after-executor listening-sockets snapshot confirms python2 process bound to *:8080 on both node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: node1 configured to load-balance incoming HTTP requests across both backends on port 80
requirements.summary: Python2 round-robin reverse proxy (lb.py) deployed as systemd service on node1, listening on 0.0.0.0:80. Repeated curl requests to node1 on both /health and /inventory alternate cleanly between node2 and node3 backends across multiple test rounds. After-executor listening-sockets snapshot confirms python2 bound to *:80 on node1.

requirements.requirement: Required firewall/network configuration allows the load-balanced traffic to flow
requirements.summary: firewalld opened 8080/tcp on node2 and node3 and 80/tcp on node1, confirmed via firewall-cmd --list-ports, and end-to-end curl tests through node1 succeeded, demonstrating the ports are actually reachable for the traffic path.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1, node2, node3) with healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For each of node2, node3, and node1 (LB last), pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged (connection drop), polling confirmed a new boot_id post-recovery, and service health plus end-to-end LB round-robin routing were re-verified afterward. Boot-identity changes are independently corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, and the final 6-request round-robin test confirms full cluster recovery.

overall_summary: The executor successfully deployed the inventory app on node2 and node3 (port 8080) and configured a working round-robin load balancer on node1 (port 80), with firewall rules opened appropriately. Round-robin behavior was directly verified through multiple rounds of curl tests both before and after a full, sequential restart of node2, node3, and node1, with boot-identity changes and service/data/cluster recovery independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is clean, with all mutations traceable to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol.
limitations: No true 'after_prepare' snapshot was captured (aliased to before_prepare since prepare was disabled), so pre-existing vs. executor-introduced state could only be compared against the before_prepare baseline, which is adequate here since prepare was not enabled.
Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at all lifecycle phases on all nodes, so no assessment of package integrity is possible; this does not affect the stated requirements.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands trace directly to the task: directory creation, application/systemd-unit writes, firewalld port openings, and the three sequential systemctl reboot operations (protocol-mandated). No abandoned files, conflicting/failed services, or unsafe exposure were observed; after-executor failed-services checks on all three nodes are empty. The only broad mutations were the three reboots, which are the mandated restart-evidence protocol and were fully verified to restore healthy state afterward. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were identified in the timeline.
